attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, written in his voice and endorsed.

semantics.note: The firm 'will take until 2028 to 2029' is kept, as is the 'any of it gets built' caveat. Treating the construction rate as an antecedent is a slight stretch, but the contract does not require that rate to stay unchanged.

contract.note: Reading the claim as aggregate deployment of the 2025–26 sales cohort is ordinary and fair. Fiscal vs calendar years, what counts as 'operationalize', and how much must stay uninstalled are all unspecified, and those choices decide the result.

evidence.note: v1 is dated May 2026, before the evaluation date. It shows one operating GB200 cluster, which meets the limited 'gets built' antecedent. As one isolated cluster it cannot settle aggregate deployment timing.
NVIDIA's own disclosure of total fiscal-2026 revenue. It contains no installation or commissioning data, so it does not bear on deployment timing.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast that runs to 2028–2029, and the deadline has not passed. Under the contract, early resolution needs representative records showing the cohort was widely deployed. The packet has only one operating cluster and NVIDIA's aggregate revenue, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary statement in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the universal 'nobody' and the qualifier 'appears'. Dropping the rhetorical 'despite all those data centers' framing is harmless. 'Appears' describes what public evidence shows, not a probability, so the claim stays an observation.

contract.note: Reading 'profit' as net profit after depreciation and financing is ordinary. Restricting the target to Q4 2025 and leaving the set of providers undefined are the evaluator's choices. Adjusted EBITDA vs net profit decides how Nebius is read.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own disclosure of a Q4 2025 GAAP net loss. It is consistent with the claim for this one provider, but it cannot establish a universal claim.
Nebius's own disclosure of positive adjusted EBITDA alongside a GAAP net loss. Positive adjusted EBITDA is not net profit, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: Both providers in the packet reported net losses, and neither shows net profit from AI rentals. Nebius's positive adjusted EBITDA does not count as net profit. Still, the claim is universal, and the packet has no comprehensive activity-level accounts. Hyperscalers and other renters are not covered at all. The evidence neither establishes the claim nor shows a profitable counterexample.
